If you want to keep up with us on our show Inner Whirled, you'll need to do the same work. These books are a value and treasure greater than a college education in comparative mythology and religious studies ever could be. Give yourself the keys of discernment. Listen to Spirit Whirled.

recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" at checkout for a 10% discount!

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements—the flowers themselves. Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

He has appeared on InnerVerse multiple times to talk about hydrogen as a macronutrient and EZ water.

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Two Self-Taught Tuners", "body": "Chance Garton came across biofield tuning around 2019 after hearing Eileen Day McCusick, author of Tuning the Human Biofield and Electric Body, Electric Health, on a handful of podcasts. Both he and host Kyle Denton learned the practice on their own rather than through the in-person and online modules McCusick certifies people with, which Chance argues is less strange than it sounds given that she was the self-taught original. He used her books as a template for biofield anatomy and kept confirming it on friends. Both men steer beginners to the 174 fork from the biofield tuning store, praising its long tines and loud, clear, lasting ring."}, {"title": "The Party Trick", "body": "Six months before this recording, Chance brought his big weighted fork, the one he nicknames Big G, to his father's house where an out-of-town cousin was visiting with back pain bad enough that he was heading to bed before seven. Sweeping the field, Chance snagged something a little past halfway in and asked about a betrayal or loss of support from the man's own father around age 27. The cousin had had exactly that falling out, never made right in his father's lifetime. The pain lifted in roughly five minutes and, Chance reports, has stayed better since. His father, who used to mock the work, stopped."}, {"title": "The Body Inside the Mind", "body": "The inversion both men circle is that the mind is not housed in the body; the body sits inside a mind distributed through the heart's toroidal field, whose outer edge corresponds to birth and which Chance divides at six years per foot. Kyle sets this against Sam Harris and the view that consciousness is an illusion thrown off by atoms colliding since the big bang, arguing such a premise would make persuasion itself pointless. Chance frames the split as the quantity versus quality dichotomy laid out by the French author and mystic Rene Guenon in The Reign of Quantity, a book he recommends with reservations about its final third."}, {"title": "Plants as Teachers", "body": "Kyle runs a clinical herbal practice and began drawing a card or striking a fork when a consultation stalled, calling it the difference between stabbing in the dark and stabbing in the light. Chance now opens sessions asking which plant teacher wants to show up, working from the Herbcrafters Tarot and the Anima astrological herbalism deck. Arnica dominates the hour: Kyle cites its traditional reputation as a rubefacient counter irritant and relates the lore that Johann Wolfgang von Goethe credited it with rescuing him late in life, while Chance reads it as the lone wolf learning to lead a pack. Kyle stresses arnica is not a plant to drink."}, {"title": "Zero Degrees Aries", "body": "Recorded on February 21, the conversation turns to Saturn and Neptune meeting at zero degrees tropical Aries, a degree that lands on Chance's natal sun. Kyle notes the last Aries pairing fell somewhere in the 500s BC, near the Athenian experiment, so astrologers concede nobody knows what to expect; Chance adds that the previous conjunction, in Capricorn, came in 1989, the year he was born. He contends the moment favors a manufactured deception and names extraterrestrial disclosure as his suspicion, arguing that the Epstein files reach into the ranks of mainstream science. His closing frame is a choice: let beliefs set your authority, or let authority hand you beliefs."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Our favorite herbalist Kyle Denton finally started his own podcast, and on this episode I’m in the guest seat. We start with one of the most interesting practitioner-to-practitioner biofield conversations you’ll hear, and by the end we’re talking about where things are headed for humanity with a surprising level of confidence.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: There are some very practical pieces here. What reading someone's field feels like, how tuning actually works, and how to work with herbs as intelligent teachers. There are also a lot of real stories, including a recent session where I cleared someone's chronic back pain in minutes. It's a good example of how simple mind-body healing can be, even with bigger issues. Along the way we cover Chance's origin story from the festival days onward, the party trick of pulling memories straight out of someone's field, a real session that clears chronic pain almost instantly, what stuck energy actually feels like in experience rather than theory, herbs like Arnica stepping in as a coach rather than a supplement, why being the nice guy can literally wreck your body, divination and synchronicity and the point where it stops feeling like coincidence, the moment you stop needing tools and simply know, and a real question worth sitting with: are your beliefs yours, or were they installed? Astrology shows up late and takes over the ending.
